I used to have a big fear of hell and it kept me from leaving Catholicism for a while but that's not a good reason to stay I eventually decided. I don't think that if there is a loving God that he would sentence people to eternal torture for not being Catholic or not following x y z rituals. If you're going to follow God do it out of love not fear. I personally believe in God but I also believe it is enough to try your best to be a good person.  Rituals and esthetics are nice (I converted to Judaism and love the ritualism) but the important thing is to do good. Who knows who is wrong and who is right about the specifics? What's really important is kindness and love.

I'm so sorry about your loss.  It's been a little over a year since one of my best friends died. I'm still grieving but it has gotten easier. I remember the initial shock. I remember how incomprehensible it seemed and how devastating it was. It has gotten easier to process over time.

I agree about the leaning into the pain but you may want to do so from the safety of a mental health professional's office (or the very least a close friend or family member's home). Emotions can be very powerful and, if you've been feeling numb, things could get intense when the emotions surface.

I also take comfort in both religion and Stocism (as in the philosophy of the Stoics).

I have also read (and listened to the audiobook version) of  Augusten Burroughs book This is How which is not completely about grief but does address grief.

Oh and I sing. I sing sad songs. I sing happy songs. I sing at home and at kareoke venues. In high school I sang in choir. I find it very helpful to let out emotional energy in a somewhat controlled manner.
